vector: identity mapping and capability set inside the workload
expected_if_secure: inner uid 1000 maps to one host subordinate uid only; CapEff 0; NoNewPrivs 1
observed: uid=1000 gid=1000 groups=[]; host-side stat shows files as 65534 (unmapped); CapEff 0, CapBnd all, NoNewPrivs 1; host uid of workload = 100001 (ps)

vector: direct write outside the workspace (/etc, $HOME, /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm)
expected_if_secure: EACCES/EROFS for every path outside workspace and artifacts
observed: all five writes returned EACCES; workspace write succeeded; /dev/null writable (documented, harmless)

vector: io_uring IORING_OP_OPENAT(O_CREAT|O_WRONLY) to bypass Landlock for direct-denied writes; also ring reads of /etc/shadow and home
expected_if_secure: ring openat denied with the same errno as direct open (Landlock is enforced on the VFS path)
observed: direct open -> PermissionError; ring openat write to /tmp, /home, /dev/shm -> -13 (EACCES); ring read of /etc/shadow -> -13; ring read of ~/.gitconfig -> fd 7 (readable, consistent with read-on-/ scope). io_uring_setup itself is available (io_uring_disabled=0).
note: io_uring is available inside the workload; the Landlock check for openat holds

vector: read operator secrets with owner-only permissions (~/.ssh, ~/.bash_history, ~/.npmrc, ~/.claude.json, /run/user/1000)
expected_if_secure: EACCES (DAC: other has no access)
observed: all denied with EACCES; /run/user/1000 denied; docker socket and pg socket dirs absent on this host

vector: read world-readable operator files under Landlock read-on-/ (ADR-013 documented limit)
expected_if_secure: documented scope: DAC protects 0600/0700 launcher files only, so 0644 files remain readable
observed: ~/.gitconfig (0644, 585 bytes) readable inside the workload; sha256 prefix 8fc21e370a60 recorded, content not kept
note: Documented in ADR-013 Limits; the claim is not met for other-readable operator files

vector: read the WSL Windows drive mount /mnt/c from inside the workload
expected_if_secure: /mnt/c is not reachable (the isolated boundary should not expose the Windows host filesystem)
observed: listing of /mnt/c succeeds (32 entries); Landlock read-on-/ covers it; no ADR entry names /mnt
note: Not listed in ADR-013 Limits; the Windows user data tree is readable by every isolated workload

vector: read the trusted server state root .sea-forge (ledgers, server.yaml, authority policy, logs, binaries)
method: probes/wl_state_read.py run inside the workload against a copy-free read of /home/sprime01/projects/sea-rs/.sea-forge
expected_if_secure: the launcher state root is not readable by a workload (0700 or equivalent); at minimum ledgers and authority policy
observed: 17 of 18 files readable: server.yaml, casework-live/cell/server.yaml, authority, ledgers, logs and binaries; only server.sock denied. Root and children are drwxr-xr-x sprime01:sprime01. Only workload-state/ and workload-slots/ get 0700 (delegation.rs from_host). No content kept; sha prefixes only.
note: Trusted control-plane state is readable by any isolated workload; write is blocked (no write permission)

vector: host pid visibility and /proc tricks (cmdline, environ, mountinfo, pid namespace)
expected_if_secure: only the workload's own pid namespace is visible; host processes (including the launcher) are invisible
observed: /proc lists only pid 1; mountinfo has 48 lines (namespace view); host launcher pid not visible; ptrace of parent gives ESRCH

vector: write /proc/sys tunables from the workload
expected_if_secure: EACCES
observed: EACCES on /proc/sys/kernel/domainname; readable /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces is 31738 (info)

vector: reach host abstract unix sockets and TCP loopback listeners started by the launcher
method: probes/wl_host_listener_probe.py with live host listeners; control: probes/host_listener_control.py (host connect succeeds)
expected_if_secure: connect refused or denied (separate netns and Landlock net denial)
observed: abstract host listener -> ECONNREFUSED; TCP 127.0.0.1:38999 -> EACCES; host-side control connects to both listeners; net ifaces inside = lo only

vector: network egress: TCP to external host, UDP/DNS to external resolver, loopback
expected_if_secure: no outbound path (net namespace with no route, Landlock TCP denial)
observed: TCP external EACCES; UDP external ENETUNREACH; TCP loopback EACCES; only lo interface exists
note: Holds only because --net is passed for every isolated launch; AllowTcpPorts would share the host netns and leave UDP and abstract sockets open (documented)

vector: cross-identity access: read, list and write another workload's workspace
method: probes/launchlib.py grant (slot 2 workspace) + probes/wl_battery2.py cross_* checks
expected_if_secure: EACCES for another identity's workspace and artifacts
observed: read secret file, list, write, and list artifacts of slot 2 all EACCES

vector: connect to another workload's MCP broker socket
method: probes/wl_symlink_mcp.py with ADV_OTHER_MCP pointing at a socket owned by slot 2
expected_if_secure: EACCES (socket ACL is identity-exclusive)
observed: connect -> EACCES

vector: nested user namespace creation and mount escalation inside the workload
expected_if_secure: nested userns may exist but cannot mount, bind or escape Landlock
observed: unshare -U succeeds (nested userns created); mount tmpfs over /home fails (uid_map / superuser); mount --bind fails; Landlock is inherited, so nothing becomes writable
note: Attack surface present (nested userns allowed); no escalation observed

vector: setuid binaries and setuid mappers reachable inside the namespace
expected_if_secure: setuid-root binaries grant nothing (root not mapped, no_new_privs set)
observed: sudo refuses: no new privileges flag set; newuidmap usage only, no mapping change possible

vector: userfaultfd and other kernel primitives for exploit staging
expected_if_secure: userfaultfd not usable by an unprivileged workload; io_uring either disabled or Landlock-confined
observed: userfaultfd -> EPERM; io_uring_setup succeeds (io_uring_disabled=0) but ring openat is Landlock-checked (ADV-A03)
note: io_uring is enabled; the surface is larger than the net/fs posture alone suggests

vector: inherited file descriptors from the launcher
expected_if_secure: only stdio and loader fds are inherited
observed: only stdio, python loader files and the probe's own ctypes library; the hand harness has no server fds, so the real server's CLOEXEC discipline is not exercised
note: Real server fd set not reproduced

vector: persistence after a normal episode end: setsid and double-fork sleepers
expected_if_secure: pid namespace ends with the episode; detached sleepers gone
observed: sleepers started with setsid and double-fork were gone after the launch returned (no uid 100001 processes)
note: kill-child holds for a normal exit

vector: launcher crash (SIGKILL) while the workload is running: orphan persistence and slot release
expected_if_secure: workload is killed when the launcher dies, or its slot stays reserved until it exits
observed: after SIGKILL of the launcher the unshare parent (pid 460935, ppid 944) and the workload shell (uid 100001) plus sleeps kept running; flock on workload-slots/1.lock was free and acquirable
note: --kill-child fires only when unshare exits; the launcher holds the slot via a File, so the slot is freed while the workload lives

vector: next episode with the same slot reuses the identity while the orphan from the prior episode runs
method: probes/lifecycle_driver.py crash, then host-side acquire + nsenter setns of the orphan's user namespace (python os.setns in probe)
expected_if_secure: a slot is not reissued while a workload under its UID is alive
observed: new acquire on slot 1 succeeded while orphan alive (both uid 100001); the orphan identity (entered by setns from a host process, so Landlock was not applied in that probe) read the next episode's workspace file and wrote into its workspace; DAC grants the same uid
note: Demonstrated at the DAC/identity level; Landlock applied to the orphan itself would still block its writes outside its own workspace but not its reads of /

vector: two concurrent acquires of the same subordinate slot
expected_if_secure: second acquisition refused while the first is held
observed: second flock refused (BlockingIOError) while the first holds it
note: Holds only while the first holder is alive (see ADV-A19/A20)

vector: symlink plant in workspace and read-through to host file; .agent-harness symlink to host home
expected_if_secure: symlinks in workspace do not reach host files for trusted readers (workload can still read host files via Landlock /)
observed: symlink plant succeeded; read through the link returned 585 bytes (host .gitconfig) from inside the workload; .agent-harness symlink to home is_dir true with entries listed
note: Workload reads are already permitted by ADV-A05; the trusted-side impact is in ADV-A23

vector: SWE_SEED harvest reads workload-controlled sparse files under .agent-harness (delegation.rs harvest_swe_seed): memory allocation driven by apparent size
method: probes/launchlib.py + host-side allocation test (512 MB sparse file, same std::fs::read pattern); code read delegation.rs:1620-1670
expected_if_secure: trusted reader rejects oversized files before allocating (size check before read)
observed: reading a 512 MB sparse file allocated and read 512 MB (maxrss delta 488 MB); harvest calls std::fs::read before the 1 MiB limit check; symlink to host home is followed by is_dir/read_dir but the error path prevents content output
note: Allocation shown via the same std::fs::read pattern; the real harvest was not executed (needs SWE_SEED configured). Launcher OOM risk on 8 GB host

vector: connect to PostgreSQL over TCP from the workload
expected_if_secure: no TCP path to the database
observed: psql -h 127.0.0.1 -> Permission denied (Landlock TCP denial, empty netns)

vector: unix socket connection as the admin role (peer auth) and guessed foreign session role
expected_if_secure: peer mapping refuses OS uid 100001 for sea_admin; unknown role refused
observed: both connections refused (peer auth / role authentication failed on the cluster)
note: Hold depends on pg_ident map=launcher; production socket_dir/pg_hba not inspected

vector: privilege probes with the brokered role: read admin table, write, CREATE TABLE, COPY to file or program, pg_read_file, lo_import, SET ROLE, ALTER ROLE SUPERUSER, CREATE EXTENSION dblink
expected_if_secure: all denied; only granted SELECT on the scope tables is allowed
observed: granted SELECT returned 2 rows; admin_secret, insert, CREATE TABLE in public, COPY TO file/program, pg_read_file, lo_import, SET ROLE sea_admin, ALTER ROLE SUPERUSER, CREATE EXTENSION all denied; TEMP table allowed (session-local)
note: Test grant set is the probe's own; the production scope grants and group roles were not reviewed

vector: exhaust the role's connection limit to bypass per-session limits or evict other sessions
expected_if_secure: limit 4 enforced for the role
observed: 6 spawned sessions: 'too many connections for role (limit 4)' enforced

vector: enumerate other sessions and roles via catalog views; read other sessions' query text
expected_if_secure: role and session metadata for other principals is hidden
observed: pg_roles lists 19 role names and pg_stat_activity shows 9 sessions to the brokered role; other sessions' query text masked (0 visible)
note: Role names of other workloads visible; no passwords or query text

vector: cross-workload covert channel via LISTEN/NOTIFY between sessions
expected_if_secure: channel either unavailable or accounted for in exposure
observed: LISTEN/NOTIFY works for the brokered role; no exposure label is recorded for DB-to-DB messaging
note: Low bandwidth; relevant only if two workloads share a database and scope

vector: backend survives VALID UNTIL expiry when the launcher is dead (no reaper)
method: probes/pg_expiry_crash_driver.py (role VALID UNTIL +15 s, workload held pg_sleep(120), launcher SIGKILLed, checked after 22 s)
expected_if_secure: the expiry reaper or process death ends the backend once VALID UNTIL passes
observed: one backend for the session role still in pg_stat_activity 22 s after expiry with no reaper; the backend ended only when its pg_sleep finished (about 120 s); the post-expiry new-login check was not completed (password prompt)
note: VALID UNTIL governs only new logins; live backends need the reaper or a server restart reconciliation. Restart reconciliation not reviewed

vector: MCP broker: frame-level tricks (duplicate keys, batches, notifications that carry tool calls, method aliases, id reuse)
method: code review of crates/sea-forge-server/src/mcp_protocol.rs parse_frame and mcp.rs dispatch/frame (existing unit test read, not executed)
expected_if_secure: every frame is validated before authority; unknown methods refused; batch members authorised one by one
observed: parse_frame rejects duplicate keys and ambiguous envelopes, caps batches at 256; dispatch allows only initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/call, tools/list; unknown methods refused (-32601); notifications with tools/call still go through authority
note: Not executed dynamically; the unit tests were read, not run

vector: exposure label gated on upstream success: classified data returned in an error or isError response is not labelled
method: code review of crates/sea-forge-server/src/mcp.rs tool_call lines 278-293 (not executed)
expected_if_secure: any classified data forwarded to the workload is recorded regardless of success
observed: registry.record runs only when the response is Ok, has no error member, and result.isError is not true; a classified tool that returns plaintext inside an error or isError payload leaves the context without that label, so later destination checks do not see it
note: Code-derived; a dynamic test with a stub upstream was not run. Fix: label on any forwarded response that carries classified output

vector: broker connection reuse and racing calls from one workload
method: code review of mcp.rs serve_workload (single accept loop, one Broker per connection, serve_stream awaited)
expected_if_secure: one in-flight call per session and no cross-connection exposure race
observed: the accept loop does not accept a second connection until the first ends, so exposure reads are serialised per socket; each connection launches a new upstream
note: Serial by construction; not exercised dynamically

vector: MCP tools that accept paths or commands: confused deputy into host files via an allowed tool
method: design review of mcp.rs tool_call (authority decides by tool name and parameters, upstream runs with launcher privileges)
expected_if_secure: upstream tools that touch host files are argument-constrained by policy
observed: authority evaluates the action with arguments, but no path or command confinement is applied to upstream processes that run as the launcher user; dependent on operator policy
note: Not tested: requires a configured upstream MCP server

vector: renewal and JIT elevation re-decision; refusal revokes live sessions
method: not executed: requires the full server, authority bundle and ledger
expected_if_secure: renewal re-decides; refusal revokes the live backend and MCP
observed: not reproduced dynamically; code paths (postgres.rs issue/expiry_reaper, mcp.rs context_revoked per call) read only

vector: exposure of classified data through workspace files, artifacts, transcript and stdout (documented limit in ADR-013)
method: design review (ADR-013 Limits; delegation.rs isolated branch writes workspace and artifacts)
expected_if_secure: documented; ADR-013 says exposure is not enforced on workspace artifacts or transcript
observed: workload writes to workspace and artifacts are unlabelled; the trusted server later reads artifacts via capture_file and the evidence dock; labels never record these channels
note: Documented limit; this remains a direct channel out of the exposure model (stdout also carries the ACP transcript)

vector: exposure via PostgreSQL labels set only at issuance (direct SQL reads)
method: design review: postgres.rs issue() records scope_exposure at grant; no per-row labelling
expected_if_secure: labels cover every class of data the scope can read
observed: labelled scope at issuance; a scope with broad SELECT labels as a whole, which over-restricts rather than leaks; writes to tables are not labelled
note: Config-dependent

vector: exposure across delegation, reconnection and transformation (sub-agent or re-spawned workload with the same case)
method: design review: delegation.rs case-wide context label Some(case:<case>) shared across items and resumed runs
expected_if_secure: labels follow the case, so a new episode inherits restrictions
observed: context is per case, so restrictions carry across items and resumed runs; a new run in the same case inherits labels (over-restricts)
note: Not executed end to end; ADV-B09 is the one label gap identified
